chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ṣalt, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
He was asked about a woman who dies while no mahram is with her. He said: Her hands are to be washed.

So the proper way regarding these reports is that we carry them upon a mode of recommendation, while the foundational ruling is what we have stated earlier: that she is buried and is not given ghusl in any circumstance. What further clarifies that will follow.

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman whose death and funerary ruling are being discussed
key_terms.مَحْرَمٌ: a person within prohibited degrees of marriage whose presence affects handling of the deceased
key_terms.يَغْسِلُ: he washes; here referring to washing in relation to the deceased

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman dies and no mahram or female relative is present to wash her?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling concerning a woman who dies when no mahram is present with her. The cited wording indicates washing her hands, but the compiler states that such reports are to be understood as recommending that act, while the basic ruling remains that she is buried without ghusl.
